purpose: Teacher-facing preview activities for the virtual classroom demo. These are suggested teaching lenses, not claims about the official unit order or exact lesson titles.
virtual_only_notice: All listed flows describe actions inside this software. They are not real-world laboratory procedures.

grade_previews.title: Classifying matter and observing a solution
grade_previews.focus: Distinguish a pure substance from a mixture and describe the visible difference between a solid and a liquid in the model.
learning_goals: Distinguish a solid sample from a liquid sample.
Recognize that a uniform solution is a mixture.
virtual_flow: Select the beaker and read its Inspector panel.
Inspect the water and salt entries in the Library and Learning Guide.
Compare the model before and after the virtual dissolution demonstration.
grade_previews.teacher_prompt: Ask students to describe what changed in appearance and what did not change about the identity of the substances.

grade_previews.title: Solute, solvent and solution formation
grade_previews.focus: Use a particle-level explanation to distinguish the solvent from the solute in a model solution.
learning_goals: Identify the solvent and solute in the classroom model.
Explain why dissolved particles are not individually visible.
virtual_flow: Select the beaker and review its contents.
Open Learning Guide and compare the observation with the explanation.
grade_previews.teacher_prompt: Ask which material acts as the solvent and how the model represents particles becoming distributed.

grade_previews.title: Saturation and conservation in a simplified model
grade_previews.focus: Discuss the idea of a solubility limit and distinguish dissolved material from a separate solid phase.
learning_goals: Define a saturated solution at a conceptual level.
Distinguish dissolved material from visible undissolved solid.
Discuss why a simulation needs stated assumptions and limits.
virtual_flow: Read the Learning Guide section on saturation.
Use the Inspector to identify the different contents and observations.
Discuss which aspects are simplified and which are represented by the software.
grade_previews.teacher_prompt: Ask students why a model must state its temperature and solubility assumptions before making quantitative claims.

grade_previews.title: Integrated view: particles, matter and energy
grade_previews.focus: Connect particle-level explanations of solutions with the temperature information displayed by the virtual model.
learning_goals: Relate a macroscopic observation to a particle-level explanation.
Distinguish a physical process from a chemical reaction.
Evaluate the limits of a simplified simulation.
virtual_flow: Select the classroom beaker and inspect the displayed temperature.
Read the explanation for dissolution and changes of state.
Compare the observed model behaviour with the stated model limitations.
grade_previews.teacher_prompt: Ask students to connect an observable change with a possible explanation at the particle level.

grade_previews.title: Evaluate a scientific model
grade_previews.focus: Treat the virtual laboratory as a scientific model: identify what it represents, what it simplifies and which curriculum pathway must be confirmed.
learning_goals: Separate a model's output from an experimentally measured value.
Explain why the exact Senior 2 pathway is required before official Chemistry mapping.
virtual_flow: Review one observation and its explanation in the Inspector.
Read the data-quality notes and curriculum status.
Compare the preview with the student's selected official pathway before using it for lesson planning.
grade_previews.teacher_prompt: Ask students which statements are direct observations, which are explanations and which are assumptions in the model.
